title: Moonsail Labs — Rapid prototyping: hosting options and credits (discovery)
summary: Intro discovery to scope a two-week rapid prototype. Customer wants to validate a low-latency recommendation endpoint and evaluate hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private. Discussed free credits for time-to-first-token (TTFT), security needs (SSO, KMS, audit logs), latency/cost tradeoffs, and a lightweight benchmark plan. Next steps: send pricing calculator, security packet, and schedule a short benchmark run (1-2 tests) next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-09 16:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood SE), Jared (Moonsail CTO), Priya (Lead ML Eng), Alex (Infra), Maya (Product)

-- Auto summary (may be rough) --
Sofia: quick run through quickstart and credits, ask about infra constraints, identify whether hosted is fine for prototype or need VPC.

00:00 - 00:30 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving time. I'm Sofia from Redwood, this is Liam and Rina. Quick agenda: understand your prototype goal, constraints, and then recommend hosted vs dedicated vs private and how to get you to first token fast.
00:31 - 01:05 Jared: Hey, thanks. So we want to build a recommender microservice for in-app suggestions, need low latency (<150ms P95 ideally), throughput maybe 20 rps to start, spiky. We want a two-week rapid prototype to validate latency and cost.
01:06 - 01:40 Priya: And we have an internal model (fine-tuned Llama variant) but open to Redwood's catalog if it's easier. Data is not PII but business-sensitive, we need audit logs and access controls.
01:41 - 02:15 Alex: We are on GCP, use KMS for keys and SSO via Okta. For production we probably need VPC peering or private endpoints, but for prototype we could try hosted if isolation and logs are good.
02:16 - 03:00 Liam: Cool. For TTFT we do a simple self-serve flow: you sign up, we give free credits, SDK + quickstart puts you to first token in under an hour for text generation. For benchmarking we'll provide a bench script; if you need private networking for the prototype we can do a VPC-based private pilot.
03:01 - 03:45 Priya: How much of the infra can be black-boxed? Our infra team wants to know only minimal network changes for a hosted flow.
03:46 - 04:20 Sofia: Hosted needs no infra changes — it's our API over TLS. You can send requests and get streaming responses. If you want private peering, that'll require a bit more setup but we can walk through.
04:21 - 05:05 Maya: What about cost estimates? Credits could cover two weeks?
05:06 - 06:00 Sofia: We'll offer pilot credits — usually enough for low-volume benchmarks. I'll share the credits table and a pricing calculator. For cost/perf tradeoffs Liam: do you want to speak to ded- vs host perf?
06:01 - 07:00 Liam: Sure — Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity -> more predictable P95 and lower variance. Hosted is multi-tenant but we've optimized routing and burst policies; for 20rps spikes dedicated might be safer for consistent latency if you need sub-150ms predictable. Also we can recommend quantized variants to reduce token cost.
07:01 - 07:40 Priya: Our model is 7B fine-tuned; will that run well in hosted?
07:41 - 08:25 Rina: Often yes; we have model catalog entries for many Llama-like families with verified profiles. If you bring your own model we can onboard it into a private bucket or via our model onboarding flow — there are some constraints on size/format.
08:26 - 09:10 Alex: Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs — are these all supported in hosted?
09:11 - 10:00 Sofia: SOC2 and audit logs yes; for SSO/SCIM we support Okta and SAML. KMS integration for private deployments; for hosted we do encryption at rest but customer-managed keys are available in Private / Dedicated VPC options. I'll attach the security pack.
10:01 - 11:00 Jared: Ok. For the benchmark, what's the minimum we need to measure?
11:01 - 12:00 Liam: We'll do three tests: cold start P95, steady-state P95 at your qps, and a spiky burst test. We'll capture token throughput, latency, and cost per token. We also instrument KV cache effectiveness if you have prefix reuse.
12:01 - 13:00 Priya: Do you support streaming for recommendations? We want partial suggestions quickly and then final ranking.
13:01 - 14:00 Rina: Yes, streaming is supported. There can be some jitter on multi-tenant hosted, but Dedicated reduces jitter. Also we have function/tool calling primitives for structured outputs if you want to emit JSON for downstream ranking.
14:01 - 15:00 Maya: Any gotchas with our GCP setup and VPC peering?
15:01 - 16:00 Liam: For VPC/private, we typically do a peering or private endpoint, need a couple firewall exceptions and routes; we'll provide a runbook. For the lightweight prototype it's optional.
16:01 - 17:00 Alex: How long to spin up a Dedicated pool?
17:01 - 18:00 Sofia: Dedicated capacity lead time depends on commitment — for a short pilot we can provision a small dedicated pool within a few days if capacity available; longer-term reserved takes planning.
18:01 - 19:00 Jared: What about data retention and logs? We need 90-day audit log retention and the ability to request exports for compliance.
19:01 - 20:00 Sofia: We support audit logs and export; retention policies and extended retention are an add-on. I'll include retention options in the packet.
20:01 - 21:00 Priya: For the model itself, can you run our fine-tuned weights? We use a custom tokenizer tweak.
21:01 - 22:00 Rina: We can onboard custom weights; tokenizer edge cases sometimes need a small adapter, we'll test. For TTFT it's fastest to use one of our catalog models and then swap in your weights for the dedicated pilot.
22:01 - 24:00 Jared: That makes sense. If we do hosted prototype with catalog model, then bring our weights for dedicated— ok.
24:01 - 25:00 Liam: On profiling — we'll enable prefix caching and see if your workload benefits; caching can drastically reduce cost for repeated prefixes.
25:01 - 27:00 Priya: How do you measure cost per call for this experiment?
27:01 - 28:00 Sofia: We'll provide a cost-per-token estimate and a sample billing forecast in the calculator; post-benchmark we'll show measured token counts and estimated monthly costs.
28:01 - 30:00 Alex: Any SLOs you provide for hosted?
30:01 - 31:00 Sofia: Hosted has best-effort but we publish performance profiles per model; Dedicated has SLA-backed latency/uptime with reserved pools. We'll include the profile links.
31:01 - 33:00 Maya: Ok wrap-up — success criteria?
33:01 - 35:00 Jared: If we can demonstrate P95 < 150ms on our steady-state and cost under X (TBD after your calc), that's a win. Also minimal infra changes for prototype.
35:01 - 37:00 Priya: Timeline: we want to run bench next week and decide by end of the month for pilot.
37:01 - 39:00 Sofia: Agreed. I'll send the security pack, credits details and pricing calc today; Liam will send a benchmark script and sample prompts. We can kick off a hosted bench immediately with the catalog model to get TTFT low.
39:01 - 41:00 Jared: Great. One more Q: do you have any examples of other retail/recommendation customers with similar latency needs?
41:01 - 42:00 Liam: Yes — I can share an anonymized case study and a short perf spreadsheet.

-- End transcript --

Notes: occasional mis-transcriptions present (Redwood Dedicate -> Dedicated, etc.). Shared artifacts: quickstart repo: https://git.redwood.ai/quickstart, security packet: https://redwood.ai/security/moonsail-pack (placeholder), pricing calc: https://redwood.ai/pilot-calc
